content:
The Laredo legal community gathered Thursday to honor 111th District Court Judge Monica Notzon as she prepares to retire after more than a decade and a half on the bench, according to KGNS.

The Laredo Bar Association hosted the retirement celebration, attended by fellow judges, elected officials, attorneys, colleagues and longtime friends, recognizing her years of public service.

Notzon was first elected to preside over the 111th District Court in 2010. Before taking the bench, she worked as an attorney in the Webb County District Attorney's Office and spent years in private practice.

According to Webb County, she was the first woman to serve as First Assistant District Attorney in Webb County. On the bench, she piloted a Mental Health Court and helped launch a pro se divorce docket.

KGNS did not report a specific date on which her retirement takes effect, nor who will succeed her. The report says only that she is preparing to step down.

Sources: KGNS, Nov. 5, 2026; Webb County, "About Judge" (webbcountytx.gov).

title: After 16 Years on the Bench, 111th District Judge Monica Notzon Prepares to Retire
